A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same CanFields work. All 16 pages of v1 and 12 pages of v2 were inspected; neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. However, v2 refers implementation details, robustness analyses, applications, and limitations to an unavailable Supplementary, limiting comparison of those portions.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction results on DeformingThings4D and CAPE, quantitative missing-region tests, timing measurements, and qualitative ablations and applications.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional DFAUST raw-scan reconstructions and quantitative component ablations in Figure 8 and Table 2.

M1.justification: The documented method retains the SIREN canonical shape, ODE-integrated low/medium-frequency velocity field, displacement/confidence consolidator, motion segmentation, and the same fitting and regularization losses. Reorganization and revised explanations do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v2 adds DFAUST raw-scan evaluation, including one_leg_loose and jumping_jacks with outliers and standing-ground artifacts. v1 only cites DFAUST, while already evaluating animal motion, clothed humans, and raw textured CAPE scans. This is a limited extension within the existing reconstruction task.

E2.justification: Motion2VecSets is newly evaluated in v2 Figure 8; NDF, DSR, OFlow, and NVFi remain the interpolation comparators. NVFi's described host pipeline changes from adapted OFlow in v1 Section 7.2 to NDF in v2 Section 7, although identical reported scores leave the underlying implementation change unresolved.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a five-sequence quantitative ablation protocol with component removal and DeepSDF/NVFi substitution controls. Its raw-scan comparison includes pretrained, fixed-length Motion2VecSets alongside methods fitted to individual sequences. The documented 10–25 input frames, 50 interpolated frames, nearest-time reference meshes, and IoU/CD/NC metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's qualitative ablations and consolidator result row, v2 Table 2 systematically quantifies the consolidator, canonical-shape frequency, velocity representation, and articulated rigidity; Figure 4 adds frequency-focused comparisons. Existing Killing, Dirichlet, and speed examples are consolidated into Figure 11. Other robustness analyses are referred to the unavailable supplement, so their deletion cannot be established.

E5.justification: Both supplied PDFs report temporal means and worst scores without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Gaussian noise levels and learned consolidator confidence scores are not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds DFAUST qualitative findings and substantial quantitative ablation results. Table 2 reports mean IoU of 83.23 for the default and 57.98 without consolidation on five sequences; these are not directly comparable to v1's broader 81.66 without-consolidator result. Common benchmark rows retain their exact values, including CanFields mean IoU of 82.84 and 84.17. Timing totals remain equivalent after rounding.

T1.justification: The constant-topology and approximately elastic/isometric assumptions, ODE flow construction, canonical pullback, network composition, and substantive loss definitions are retained. Splitting the total objective into canonical and velocity energies merely regroups existing terms. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: Despite the new title and greater raw-scan emphasis, the central contributions remain unsupervised coherent reconstruction through dynamic consolidation and separation of detailed geometry from smooth deformation. Robustness, tracking, and efficiency claims were already present; the added experiments principally provide supporting evidence.

C2.justification: v2 replaces v1's adversarial-training interpretation with curriculum learning and attributes fitting imbalance specifically to slower ODE-based flow training. It adds interpretations concerning incompressibility and avoiding zero-velocity singularities without new derivations, and qualifies Motion2VecSets' raw-scan underperformance by its training mismatch.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Poisson-disk preprocessing, 10K Gaussian ambient samples, and 20GB peak memory, and states that code accompanies the supplement with public release planned upon acceptance. However, v1's architecture details, solver tolerances, optimizer settings, learning rates, and schedules cannot be matched against v2's unavailable implementation supplement. Whether these details were retained or revised remains unresolved.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands research positioning, dividing flow methods into predefined-template and learned-canonical approaches and discussing their relationships to Neural ODEs and bidirectional mappings. Newly discussed works include Motion2VecSets, CaDeX, 4DRecons, RFNet-4D, and several Gaussian reconstruction methods, beyond bibliographic or citation-style updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related work are extensively rewritten. The method narrative changes from velocity design, fitting, and consolidation to the fitting problem, consolidation, frequency decoupling, and training pipeline. Detailed implementation, applications, and limitations sections are replaced largely by supplementary references.

P2.justification: v2 introduces a raw-scan teaser, Figures 4 and 8, and the quantitative ablation table. It merges v1 Tables 1–2 into Table 1, condenses Figures 8–9 into Figure 9, and combines three regularization figures into Figure 11. Other figures are cropped or redrawn, and the timing table gains categories and stage breakdowns.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens component validation through Table 2, adds challenging DFAUST examples, and provides a clearer narrative. However, v1's self-contained implementation and detailed robustness/failure evidence are displaced by an unavailable supplement. The changed NVFi adaptation description alongside identical scores also leaves comparison provenance unclear. These gains and unresolved losses prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
